A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GLEAM research work. Their complete main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–D are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulation experiments evaluating exploration policies on 128 unseen scenes, alongside ablations, noise robustness tests, and the trajectory-reward experiment in Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark results, ablations, noise robustness tests, and Appendix D experiment.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Appendices B–C retain the same semantic maps, LocoTransformer encoder, A*-verified long-term goals, PPO objectives, and randomized training strategies.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same GLEAM-Bench scenes from ProcTHOR, HSSD, Gibson, and Matterport3D. The evaluated active-mapping tasks and noise scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 3 retains Random, Vacuum, FBE, UPEN, ANM, ANS, and OccAnt. Comparator subsets in the trajectory and qualitative comparisons, and baseline adaptations in Appendix B.4, also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Both retain the 1,024/128 training/test split, 50-keyframe evaluation budget, coverage/AUC/Chamfer-distance metrics, and the same training, camera, preprocessing, and noise-test settings.

E4.justification: Tables 4–5 and Figure 5 retain the training-data and component ablations. Table 7 retains the noise robustness tests, and Appendix D.1/Table 10 retains the trajectory-efficiency reward analysis.

E5.justification: Table 3 reports averages over 10 evaluation episodes per scene in both versions. Run-count disclosures and statistical reporting are unchanged; no confidence intervals or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: All reported numerical and qualitative results match. For example, Table 3 reports GLEAM's overall coverage of 66.50%, AUC of 57.63%, and Chamfer distance of 0.80 m in both versions; the appendix results also match.

T1.justification: The occupancy log-odds formulation and derivation, coverage and reward definitions, and PPO objectives in Equations 1–6 are unchanged. No assumptions, proofs, or other formal results are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about GLEAM-Bench, generalizable exploration, and superiority over existing active-mapping baselines.

C2.justification: The explanations of generalization and component effectiveness remain unchanged. Section 5.5 retains the same limitations concerning sensor noise, pose drift, dynamic environments, complex 3D surfaces, multi-floor scenes, and multi-agent deployment.

D1.justification: The implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware and training-time disclosures, preprocessing instructions, project link, and promised release of export scripts and assets are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, the research-positioning statements, and all 55 bibliography entries are unchanged. The new personal acknowledgment does not introduce a cited work or revise the relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: The acknowledgments add the National Key R&D Program of China grant 2022ZD0160201 and thank Gang Chen for drone-control guidance, with small wording edits. The arXiv version/date header changes; scientific prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The expanded acknowledgments locally reflow page 10, and small typographic spacing differences appear in table headings. Figures 1–7 and Tables 1–10 retain their structure, placement, captions, and substantive content.

improvement.justification: v2 makes funding and contributor acknowledgments more complete, but the scientific content, evidence, reproducibility information, and limitations remain unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. These administrative and small typographic edits do not materially alter overall paper quality.
